title: optimize cpu request path: reduce serialization, partition threadpools, and optional core pinning
description: Motivation: We observe CPU-side bottlenecks on the request path for small-batch, low-latency workloads. Hot paths include request serialization/deserialization, contention in the global thread pool, and OS-level thread migrations that increase tail latency. This PR introduces several targeted optimizations: 1) reduce serialization overhead by switching to a compact TLV-style wire format for internal RPCs and enabling zero-copy payload handoff between the IO layer and worker queues; 2) partition the global thread pool into IO and CPU worker pools with per-shard queues to reduce lock contention and improve cache locality; 3) optional thread/core pinning (linux sched_setaffinity) with a runtime flag so deployments can pin latency-sensitive threads to reserved cores; 4) KV cache read-path micro-optimizations (read-side prefetching, switch to a shared-read lock with optimistic fast-path) to minimize blocking during cache hits; 5) continuous-batching path changes: replace the contended mutex-backed batching queue with a lock-free ring buffer and batched dequeuing to reduce scheduling overhead. The description below summarizes the changes, rationale, and rollout plan. Implementation details: New runtime flags: --pin-main-threads (bool), --io-workers=N, --cpu-workers-per-shard=N, --cpu-worker-cores=list. These are no-op unless set and default to previous behavior to preserve compatibility. Serialization: introduce internal tlv::Frame and use zero-copy slices for payloads where possible; RPC framing is now 8-16 bytes smaller on average. Thread pools: implement PartitionedThreadPool with N shards; each has its own work-stealing ring; IO threads only enqueue minimal work items and hand off ownership of buffers to CPU workers. KV cache: add Cache::prefetch_read and a fast-path read that avoids write-lock acquisition on common hits. Continuous batching: LockFreeBatchQueue uses atomic head/tail with single-writer enqueue and multi-reader batched pop. Benchmarks: microbenchmarks run on c6i.large (2 vCPU) and c6i.4xlarge (16 vCPU) representative instances show: small request latency (p50) improved by 22% on 2-vCPU instances; p99 improved by 16% in steady-state for mixed workloads; throughput for small-batch workloads improved by up to 1.9x when CPU workers were pinned to dedicated cores. Safety and compatibility: All changes are behind runtime flags and feature gates. Default rollout preserves existing behavior. The KV cache optimization includes a fallback slow-path identical to previous semantics. Testing: Unit tests for serialization, threadpool invariants, and KV cache correctness; integration tests in perf-canary harness showing stable latency at 5% canary; stress test suite run in CI. Rollout plan: 1) Merge to main behind feature flag. 2) Canary rollout at 5% traffic with monitoring dashboards (latency, CPU steal, scheduling stalls). 3) Gradually increase to 25% and 100% with rollback window. Related work: ENG-2374 (request path profiling), ENG-2421 (continuous batching redesign), SRE-501 (incident followup for high p99 on small instances).
